title: Juno app catalog
description: What a streaming service is called on every box that has it, and the string each platform needs to launch it. A controller reads this so a room can offer `Netflix` once instead of offering the Roku's Netflix and the Apple TV's Netflix as two different things, and so a driver can launch an app on a device that will not say what it has installed.

platforms.description: Documentation only: what a `launch` value means for each platform key, so somebody filling one in knows whether it wants a package name, a numeric id, or a display name. Not read by a controller — the value is opaque to core, and only the driver for that platform interprets it.

slug.description: Stable id. Never change or reuse one — a project may have written it down.

name.description: What a person is shown, and what a room is asked for. Matched as an alias automatically.

aliases.description: The other spellings, matched case- and punctuation-insensitively: what each vendor's own app list calls it, and what somebody would say out loud. Only the ones that differ from `name` and `slug`. Matching is exact rather than fuzzy on purpose, so `Netflix Kids` stays its own app — a miss is fixed by adding a spelling here, which every house then gets, rather than by loosening a rule for everybody.

icon.description: Artwork for this service, as a URL to the brand's own published icon — nothing is redistributed from this repository, and a controller fetches it and hands it on so a phone that is not on the house network still sees it. Only needed for a *platform* that cannot list what it has installed: a Roku or an Apple TV reports its own channels with its own artwork, and that always wins. In practice that means a SmartCast set, so most of these come from VIZIO's own app image API, joined to `vizio_apps_prod.json` by `id`. Sparse — an absent icon draws the service's initials, which is honest and is what every regional broadcaster here gets until somebody adds one.

launch.description: Per platform, the string that opens this app. Sparse: an absent platform means nobody has filled that one in, not that the app is unavailable there — and a device that lists its own apps needs none of this. Opaque to core, which only works out which platform a device is and hands the value to its driver.
